paper.title: Improved Regret Bounds for Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound in Bayesian Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian optimization (Bayesian GP bandit) with Matérn kernel
unmapped: Objective f is a sample path of a known zero-mean GP (not an RKHS-norm-bounded function)
Domain is [0,r]^d; the learner knows r and the sample-path Lipschitz constants a, b used in beta_t
Learner knows lengthscale and smoothness nu of the kernel
settings.definition_quote: Let $f: \mX \rightarrow \R$ be a black-box objective function whose input domain $\mX$ is $\mX \coloneqq [0, r]^d$ ... We consider a Bayesian setting, where the objective function $f$ and the noise sequence $(\epsilon_t)$ are drawn from a known zero-mean Gaussian process (GP) and a Gaussian distribution, respectively.

source.quote:
Suppose Assumptions~ef{asmp:func} and ef{asmp:noise} hold. Set $k = \sek$ or $k = \matk$ with $
u > 2$. ... Then, with probability at least $1 - \dGP - \delta$, the cumulative regret of GP-UCB satisfies $R_T = 	ilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ if $k = \matk$ with $2
u + d \leq 
u^2$, $O(\sqrt{T \ln^2 T})$ if $k = \sek$.

results.notes: Regret is realized regret sum f(x*) - f(x_t) on a GP sample path, bounded with high probability over prior and noise (Bayesian high-probability regret). Not a bound on expected Bayesian regret. Dependence 'worst_case' in the sense that it only depends on T (constants depend on the sample path).

source.label: thm:cr_gp-ucb
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{asmp:func} and \ref{asmp:noise} hold. Set $k = \sek$ or $k = \matk$ with $\nu > 2$. ... Then, with probability at least $1 - \dGP - \delta$, the cumulative regret of GP-UCB satisfies ... $O(\sqrt{T \ln^2 T})$ if $k = \sek$.

results.notes: Improves O(sqrt(T ln^{d+2} T)) of Srinivas et al. Bayesian high-probability regret on the sample path.
